stem:
Tanya buys apples grown in a nearby orchard instead of apples trucked from far away. Food miles are the travel from producer to consumer.

Why can eating more local food help?

options.text: Any food labelled local always has fewer food miles, even after a long detour.
Shorter producer-to-consumer travel means fewer food miles, which can cut cost and pollution.
Putting the same far-away apples on sale reduces their food miles even if the truck route stays the same.
Food miles stop when the apples leave the orchard, so later travel does not count.

teacher.key_rationale: Local food shortens producer-to-consumer travel, so food miles fall and cost and pollution can fall with them.
